security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown syntax, public service discovery, or expected authentication; no evidence found of prompt injection or unrelated credential exfiltration. Confirmed risks include optional plaintext proxy authentication, unsafe token-file replacement, and recovery signatures in process arguments. Some documented curl examples also print replacement tokens despite nearby secrecy warnings.

remediation.issue: Legacy transports expose reusable authentication tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Require verified TLS CONNECT or an independently encrypted tunnel; remove runnable plaintext examples and never use legacy transports on untrusted networks.

remediation.issue: Token writers follow symlinks and update destination permissions after writing.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary file in a verified owned directory, reject unsafe destinations, write using a secured descriptor, and atomically replace the token.

remediation.issue: Rotation and recovery examples print raw token-bearing responses.
remediation.suggestion: Replace raw curl examples with the helper or parse responses privately, store tokens, and emit only explicitly selected non-secret fields.

remediation.issue: Recovery signatures appear in helper and Python process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Read recovery signatures from stdin or a private file and build recovery bodies without placing signatures in subprocess arguments or command history.

content.user_title: Manage Paid Proxy Egress With x402socks
content.value_statement: Agents may need regional egress without a subscription account. This skill guides approved USDC purchases and provides helpers for proxy discovery, credential management, and connection testing.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve service health, package catalogs, and healthy enabled proxy exits.
Decode live payment challenges and compare quoted amounts against a configured USDC cap.
Provide TypeScript payment guidance with approved recipient, asset, network, domain, scheme, and amount checks.
Save access tokens and request rotation or wallet-signed recovery through a shell helper.
Check token validity, account status, and usage through documented service endpoints.
Test egress through TLS CONNECT and provide curl, Python, Node, and browser proxy examples.
limitations: Purchases require a funded Base wallet, external payment libraries, and explicit authorization.
The shell helper has no purchase command; Python payment examples require additional signer and transport integration.
Prices, exits, quotas, and concurrency limits depend on the external service; proxy routing does not guarantee anonymity or target access.
Legacy transports expose tokens; token-file replacement, recovery arguments, and raw-response examples require security hardening.

use_cases.title: Verify Regional Application Access
use_cases.description: Choose a healthy regional TLS exit and verify egress before testing an application you are authorized to access.

use_cases.title: Budget Short Proxy Sessions
use_cases.description: Compare current packages, review payment terms, and request approval before authorizing a limited proxy session.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Existing Proxy Credentials
use_cases.description: Check token validity, usage, and exit health before rotating credentials or recovering access after a settled payment.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Service Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use x402socks to check service health and list healthy enabled exits. Do not purchase access or read wallet secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Limited Budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote the current six-hour package against a $1 maximum. Summarize all payment terms and wait for my approval before signing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an approval without spending.

prompt_templates.title: Validate TLS Egress
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing token file to validate access and test a healthy TLS CONNECT exit. Report the egress IP without printing credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: test existing access without a purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Guarded Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a TypeScript purchase using my approved terms. Bind signing to the approved amount, recipient, asset, network, scheme, and domain. Require confirmation before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review payment authorization and secure token capture.

output_examples.input: Quote a six-hour package against a $0.50 maximum.
output: Illustrative result: The live challenge requests $1.00 for the six-hour package.
The requested amount exceeds the approved $0.50 maximum.
No payment was authorized. A new approval is required.

output_examples.input: Summarize an existing token validation and TLS egress test.
output: Selected exit: eu-north1. Transport: TLS CONNECT on port 3129.
The egress address differs from the direct address. No token value is included.

output_examples.input: Explain what to do after payment settled but provisioning failed.
output_examples.output: Do not purchase again. Keep the settlement transaction hash and recover access with a fresh signature from the paying wallet.

best_practices: Approve complete payment terms and enforce them against the exact challenge selected for signing.
Use verified TLS CONNECT and keep credentials out of transcripts, process arguments, and source control.
Check live exit health and token validity before retrying; recover settled purchases instead of paying twice.
anti_patterns: Allowing unattended payment wrappers to sign unapproved or changed payment requirements.
Using plaintext proxy authentication or disabling certificate verification to bypass connection failures.
Printing replacement tokens, exposing recovery signatures in arguments, or saving credentials through unsafe file paths.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Helper commands require shell access, curl, and usually Python 3.

faq.question: Does the helper purchase access automatically?
faq.answer: No. It quotes packages and manages existing credentials. Purchases require an external x402 client and explicit approval.

faq.question: What currency and network does the workflow use?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses USDC on Base. Validate the live challenge against approved asset, network, recipient, domain, scheme, and amount.

faq.question: Are SOCKS5 credentials encrypted?
faq.answer: Not on the documented legacy connection. SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose the reusable token; prefer verified TLS CONNECT.

faq.question: Can lost access be recovered without paying again?
faq.answer: The documented recovery flow uses the settlement transaction hash and a fresh signature from the paying wallet, subject to account eligibility.

faq.question: Does changing the exit IP guarantee access or anonymity?
faq.answer: No. Targets can still restrict access, service quotas still apply, and a proxy does not replace authorization or privacy safeguards.
